assumptions: The existing codebase is built on Spring Framework 6.0+ and Java 17+, so all new features are compatible with the existing runtime environment.
ZooKeeper is already deployed and integrated into the system for metadata storage, so no new ZK cluster provisioning or core ZK client changes are required.
The existing xd-shell and Admin server have extensible Spring Security and connection logic that can be modified without full rewrites.
Pre-built OpenCV native libraries are available for all target deployment platforms (Linux, Windows, macOS) via the JNI wrapper, eliminating the need for custom platform-specific native builds.
The Kafka 0.9 consumer rewrite only modifies the consumer client interface, with no breaking changes to the existing message format or producer API.
The existing CI/CD pipeline already supports GitFlow branching patterns, so maintenance branch setup only requires configuration changes rather than new pipeline development.
All user stories are independent with no cross-cutting dependencies that would require additional coordination or integration effort beyond the listed activities.
The existing test suite has sufficient coverage for the modules being modified, so no new test infrastructure is required.

activities.activity_name: Design ZK tenant namespace scoping logic
activities.activity_description: Design the mapping between tenant profiles and ZooKeeper path prefixes to ensure metadata isolation between tenants, with no cross-tenant access allowed.
Modify the existing ZooKeeper client wrapper to automatically prepend tenant-specific namespace prefixes to all ZK path operations, ensuring transparent isolation for existing code.
Write and run unit and integration tests to verify that tenants can only access their own namespaced metadata, and cross-tenant access is blocked.
Design the form-based login flow for the Admin server using Spring Security, with no persistent credential storage to avoid password logging risks.
Implement the login endpoint, credential validation, and session management for the Admin server, ensuring credentials are only stored in temporary HTTP sessions and never logged or persisted.
Write and run security tests to verify invalid credentials are rejected, valid credentials grant access, and no credentials are exposed in logs or persistent storage.
Create the dedicated 'maintenance' branch from the latest minor release tag in version control, and set up branch protection rules to only allow merge requests for patch/minor version changes.
Create documentation for the development team outlining when to use the maintenance branch vs master, and the PR/merge process for maintenance branch changes.
Run static code analysis (SonarQube) scans of the module registry, Shell, and Admin-UI codebases to generate a list of deprecated functions and unused code for removal.
Delete deprecated module definition download APIs and all unused code identified in the scan, ensuring no broken references remain in the codebase.
Run the full unit, integration, and system test suite to verify that the code cleanup has not introduced any regressions.

Write and run tests to verify the admin server correctly writes its port to ZK on startup, and xd-shell can successfully connect to the admin server using the discovered port.
Update all Maven/Gradle dependencies to use Kafka 0.9.x client libraries, resolving any version conflicts with existing dependencies.

Research Motion-JPEG format specifications, test streaming performance and compatibility with the existing data ingest pipeline, and document feasibility findings.

activities.activity_name: Integrate OpenCV JNI wrapper for frame processing
activities.activity_description: Add the platform-agnostic OpenCV JNI wrapper dependency, implement video frame capture and processing logic for facial detection, and test functionality across target deployment platforms.
Create an HTTP endpoint that streams captured video frames in Motion-JPEG format, integrated with the existing data ingest pipeline for downstream predictive analytics processing.
Write and run tests to verify the streaming endpoint outputs valid Motion-JPEG frames, and frame processing works correctly for the facial detection use case.
